column50: The paper proposes BGNN4VD, a function-level GNN-based C/C++ vulnerability detector. The paper uses multiple graph representations of source code (e.g., AST, CFG, DFG) to extract syntax and sematic information. In particular, they combine AST, CFG, and DFG into so-called code composite graph (CCG) which is used as the underlying graph for the GNN. The nodes are vectorized using word2vec and fed (with the node type) as an input to a bidirectional graph neual network (BGNN). The motivation behind idirectionality is that the GNN should be able to deal with the code sequences both in the forward and backward direction to obtain a deeper representation, The BGNN outputs final node embeddings, which are then fed as an input to CNN classifier that detects vulnerabilities. BGNN4VD was shown to outperform SySeVR, VUDDY, Flawfinder, and RATS.

column50: This paper proposes DeepDFA, a vulnerability detector based on GNNs aiming of simulating data flow analysis. They utilize the CFG as the underlying graph for GNN, and use the bit-vector representation of dataflow facts to encode definitions and uses of variables (abstract dataflow embedding), which makes a GNN simulates or equivalent to DFA. DeepDFA achieves remarkable accuracy using so little data as 50+ vulnerable samples, and so little time as 9 minutes to train. DeepDFA performs better than non-transformer baselines, and when combined with UniXCoder, outperforms all baselines on the Big-Vul dataset. The combination happens by concatenating graph embedding from DeePDFA and sentence embedding from LLM, and feeding it to feed forward MLP. DeepDFA also outperforms all baselines on detecting vulnerabilities in projects on which it was not trained. Authors claim the superior performance is due to that their embedding does not include any irrelevant info, but only info related to vulnerabilities (i.e., abstract dataflow embedding).
